name: Availability Bitmask Cache Layer
description: Builds and maintains Redis-cached bitmasks from PostgreSQL availability_blocks data. On cache miss: queries all availability blocks for a unit within a 366-day window (to handle leap years), constructs a bitmask (1=available, 0=blocked), stores in Redis with configurable TTL. On availability update: invalidates the cached bitmask (lazy rebuild on next read). Key format: avail:{CRC32C(unit_id) % 64}:{unit_id}. Internal bitmask is a raw Redis bit string of 366 bits anchored to today's UTC date (bit 0 = today, bit 365 = today + 365 days). Anchor date staleness is detected on reads: if the cached bitmask's anchor date differs from today's UTC date, the cache entry is treated as a miss and rebuilt. Singleflight pattern prevents thundering herd on concurrent cache misses for the same unit. Redis unavailability triggers graceful degradation to direct PostgreSQL queries (logged as warning). Exposes checkAvailability, checkBulkAvailability, and invalidateCache.

types.name: UnitId
types.description: Branded UUID v4 string identifying a bookable unit. Must conform to lowercase UUID v4 format (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits with hyphens). Acts as a nominal/branded type to prevent accidental interchange with other string identifiers.

types.name: DateString
types.description: Branded ISO 8601 date string in YYYY-MM-DD format, UTC-anchored. No time component. Must represent a valid calendar date. Acts as a nominal/branded type to prevent accidental interchange with other strings.

types.name: ShardKey
types.description: Branded integer in the range [0, 63] inclusive, derived from CRC32C(unit_id) % shardCount. Used as the hash slot in the Redis key format: avail:{shard}:{unit_id}. Constrains key distribution to a fixed number of Redis hash slots for predictable cluster behavior.

types.name: HashAlgorithm
types.description: Supported hash algorithms for shard key derivation.

types.name: CacheConfig

fields.name: ttl_seconds
fields.description: Time-to-live in seconds for cached bitmask entries in Redis. After expiry, next read triggers a lazy rebuild from PostgreSQL.

validators.error_message: TTL must be between 1 second and 86400 seconds (24 hours).

fields.name: shard_count
fields.description: Number of shard buckets for key distribution. CRC32C(unit_id) % shard_count produces the ShardKey. Must be a power of 2 for uniform distribution.

validators.error_message: Shard count must be between 1 and 1024.
Shard count must be a power of 2.

fields.name: window_days
fields.description: Total number of bits in the bitmask representing the availability window starting from today's UTC date. Default 366 to handle leap years (bit 0 = today, bit 365 = today + 365 days).

validators.error_message: Window days must be between 1 and 731.

fields.name: hash_algorithm
fields.description: Hash algorithm used to derive the shard key from unit_id. Currently only CRC32C is supported.

fields.name: key_prefix
fields.description: Prefix for all Redis keys produced by this cache layer. Key format: {key_prefix}:{shard}:{unit_id}.

validators.error_message: Key prefix must be 1-16 lowercase alphanumeric characters starting with a letter.

fields.name: singleflight_enabled
fields.description: When true, concurrent cache misses for the same unit_id are coalesced into a single PostgreSQL query (singleflight/request-collapsing pattern) to prevent thundering herd.

fields.name: fallback_to_pg_on_redis_failure
fields.description: When true, Redis unavailability triggers graceful degradation to direct PostgreSQL queries. A warning-level log is emitted. When false, CacheUnavailable error is returned.

types.description: Configuration for the Availability Bitmask Cache Layer. Immutable after construction.

fields.name: message

fields.name: unit_id

fields.name: message
fields.description: Human-readable message including Redis connection details (sanitized).

fields.name: redis_error

fields.name: message
fields.description: Human-readable message.

types.description: Catch-all error for unexpected failures (e.g., corrupt bitmask, PostgreSQL query timeout, singleflight panic).

types.description: Discriminated union of all error types produced by the Availability Bitmask Cache Layer. Discriminant field is error_code.

types.name: AvailabilityResult

fields.name: ok
fields.description: True if the operation succeeded, false if an error occurred.

fields.name: value
fields.description: True if the entire date range [startDate, endDate] is available (all bits = 1). Only meaningful when ok=true.

fields.name: error
fields.description: The error that occurred. Only present when ok=false.

types.description: Result wrapper for checkAvailability. Discriminated on 'ok' field: if ok=true, value contains the boolean availability; if ok=false, error contains the AvailabilityError.

types.name: BulkUnitResult

fields.name: unit_id
fields.description: The unit this result pertains to.

fields.name: available
fields.description: True if the entire date range is available for this unit. Null/false if an error occurred for this specific unit.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Per-unit error if this unit's lookup failed (e.g., UnitNotFound). Null if lookup succeeded.

types.description: Per-unit result within a bulk availability check. Supports per-unit error granularity: a unit may be available (true), unavailable (false), or errored (null with error populated).

types.name: BulkUnitResultList
types.description: List of per-unit results from a bulk availability check.

types.name: BulkAvailabilityResult

fields.name: ok
fields.description: True if the bulk operation completed (individual units may still have errors). False only on systemic failure.

fields.name: results
fields.description: Per-unit availability results. One entry per requested unit_id, in the same order as the input. Only present when ok=true.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Systemic error affecting all units. Only present when ok=false.

types.description: Result wrapper for checkBulkAvailability. On success, results contains a list of per-unit availability outcomes (including per-unit errors). A top-level error indicates a systemic failure affecting all units (e.g., both Redis and PostgreSQL down).

types.name: InvalidationResult

fields.name: ok
fields.description: True if the invalidation succeeded (or key did not exist). False if an error occurred.

fields.name: error
fields.description: The error that occurred. Only present when ok=false.

types.description: Result wrapper for invalidateCache. On success, value is None (void). On failure, error describes what went wrong.

types.name: UnitIdList
types.description: List of UnitId values for bulk operations.

types.name: RedisClient

fields.name: get_bit
fields.description: Async method: (key: str, offset: int) → int. Returns the bit value (0 or 1) at the given offset in the string stored at key.

fields.name: get_bit_range
fields.description: Async method: (key: str, start_offset: int, end_offset: int) → bytes. Returns the raw bytes covering bits [start_offset, end_offset]. Caller must mask boundary bits.

fields.name: set_bits
fields.description: Async method: (key: str, bit_map: dict[int, int], ttl_seconds: int) → None. Sets multiple bits atomically via MULTI/EXEC pipeline, then sets TTL.

fields.name: delete_key
fields.description: Async method: (key: str) → bool. Deletes the key. Returns true if key existed, false otherwise.

fields.name: pipeline_get_bit_ranges
fields.description: Async method: (commands: list[tuple[str, int, int]]) → list[bytes]. Executes multiple GETRANGE commands in a single Redis pipeline for bulk operations.

fields.name: exists
fields.description: Async method: (key: str) → bool. Returns true if key exists in Redis.

fields.name: get_key_metadata
fields.description: Async method: (key: str) → dict. Returns metadata including TTL remaining and anchor_date stored alongside the bitmask.

fields.name: ping
fields.description: Async method: () → bool. Health check. Returns true if Redis is reachable.

types.description: Dependency injection abstraction for the Redis client. Consumers inject an implementation conforming to this interface. Supports single-key and pipelined bit operations. All methods are async. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

fields.name: unit_id
fields.description: The unit this block belongs to.

fields.name: start_date
fields.description: Inclusive start date of the block.

fields.name: end_date
fields.description: Inclusive end date of the block.

fields.name: is_available
fields.description: True if the unit is available during this block, false if blocked.

types.description: A single availability block record from PostgreSQL. Represents a contiguous date range during which a unit is either available or blocked.

types.name: AvailabilityBlockList
types.description: List of availability blocks returned from PostgreSQL queries.

types.name: PgClient

fields.name: get_availability_blocks
fields.description: Async method: (unit_id: UnitId, range_start: DateString, range_end: DateString) → AvailabilityBlockList. Returns all availability_blocks rows overlapping the given date range for the specified unit. Returns empty list if unit_id has no blocks (caller must distinguish from unit-not-found via unit_exists).

fields.name: unit_exists
fields.description: Async method: (unit_id: UnitId) → bool. Returns true if the unit_id exists in the units table.

fields.name: get_availability_blocks_bulk
fields.description: Async method: (unit_ids: list[UnitId], range_start: DateString, range_end: DateString) → dict[UnitId, AvailabilityBlockList]. Batch query returning availability blocks grouped by unit_id.

fields.name: ping
fields.description: Async method: () → bool. Health check. Returns true if PostgreSQL is reachable.

types.description: Dependency injection abstraction for the PostgreSQL client. Consumers inject an implementation conforming to this interface. All methods are async. Used as the source of truth for availability data.

types.name: BitmaskMetadata

fields.name: anchor_date
fields.description: The UTC date representing bit 0 of the bitmask. If this differs from today's UTC date on a read, the cache entry is stale and treated as a miss.

fields.name: built_at_epoch_ms
fields.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the bitmask was constructed. Used for observability and debugging.

fields.name: window_days
fields.description: Number of bits in the bitmask. Must match CacheConfig.window_days.

types.description: Internal metadata stored alongside each cached bitmask in Redis (as a separate hash field or encoded prefix). Used for anchor date staleness detection.

functions.name: checkAvailability
functions.description: Checks whether a single unit is fully available for an inclusive date range [startDate, endDate]. On cache hit with a valid (non-stale) bitmask: performs O(1) bitwise AND check across the relevant bit range. On cache miss or stale anchor date: queries PostgreSQL for all availability_blocks within the 366-day window, constructs the bitmask, stores in Redis with TTL, then checks the requested range. Singleflight pattern coalesces concurrent misses for the same unit_id. If Redis is unavailable and fallback_to_pg_on_redis_failure is true, queries PostgreSQL directly (logged as warning). Single-day queries (startDate == endDate) are supported.

inputs.name: unit_id
inputs.description: The UUID of the bookable unit to check availability for.

validators.error_message: unit_id must be a valid lowercase UUID v4.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.description: Inclusive start date of the range to check. Must be today (UTC) or in the future.

validators.error_message: start_date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.description: Inclusive end date of the range to check. Must be >= start_date and within the window_days from today.

validators.error_message: end_date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format.

error_cases.name: invalid_date_format
error_cases.condition: start_date or end_date does not parse to a valid calendar date (e.g., 2024-02-30)

error_cases.name: unit_not_found
error_cases.condition: unit_id does not exist in PostgreSQL units table (checked during cache rebuild only)

error_cases.name: cache_unavailable
error_cases.condition: Redis is unreachable AND fallback_to_pg_on_redis_failure is false

error_cases.name: internal_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected failure: corrupt bitmask, PostgreSQL timeout, singleflight panic, or both Redis and PostgreSQL are unreachable

preconditions: unit_id is a valid UUID v4 string.
start_date and end_date are valid ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD date strings representing real calendar dates.
start_date >= today (UTC). 'Today' is defined as the current date at UTC midnight.
At least one of RedisClient or PgClient is reachable.
postconditions: If ok=true, value is true if and only if every date in [start_date, end_date] inclusive has bit=1 in the bitmask (or equivalent PostgreSQL check on fallback).
If ok=true, value is false if any date in [start_date, end_date] has bit=0.
If the bitmask was rebuilt from PostgreSQL, it is now cached in Redis with the configured TTL (unless Redis is unavailable).
If the cached bitmask had a stale anchor_date (not equal to today UTC), it was treated as a miss and rebuilt.
If singleflight was active, only one PostgreSQL query was issued for concurrent callers requesting the same unit_id.
side_effects: On cache miss: issues a SELECT query to PostgreSQL availability_blocks table.
On cache miss: writes the rebuilt bitmask and metadata to Redis with configured TTL.
On stale anchor date detection: deletes stale key and rebuilds (equivalent to miss).
On Redis failure with fallback enabled: emits a warning-level log.
Singleflight: may block concurrent callers for the same unit_id until the first caller's rebuild completes.

functions.name: checkBulkAvailability
functions.description: Checks availability for multiple units across the same inclusive date range [startDate, endDate]. Uses a Redis pipeline to fetch bitmasks for all requested units in a single round-trip. Units with cache misses are batch-queried from PostgreSQL. Returns per-unit results with per-unit error granularity: individual units may fail (e.g., UnitNotFound) without failing the entire batch. A top-level error (ok=false) indicates systemic failure affecting all units.

inputs.name: unit_ids
inputs.description: List of unit UUIDs to check. Must contain at least 1 and at most 100 unit_ids. Duplicates are deduplicated internally.

validators.error_message: unit_ids must contain between 1 and 100 entries.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.description: Inclusive start date of the range to check. Must be today (UTC) or in the future.

validators.error_message: start_date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.description: Inclusive end date of the range to check. Must be >= start_date and within window_days from today.

validators.error_message: end_date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format.

error_cases.name: invalid_date_format
error_cases.condition: start_date or end_date does not parse to a valid calendar date

error_cases.name: too_many_unit_ids
error_cases.condition: unit_ids list contains more than 100 entries

error_cases.name: systemic_cache_unavailable
error_cases.condition: Redis is unreachable AND PostgreSQL is unreachable

error_cases.name: internal_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected systemic failure affecting all units

preconditions: All unit_ids are valid UUID v4 strings.
start_date and end_date are valid ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD date strings representing real calendar dates.
unit_ids list is non-empty and contains at most 100 entries.
At least one of RedisClient or PgClient is reachable.
postconditions: If ok=true, results contains exactly one BulkUnitResult per unique unit_id from the input, in input order (deduped).
For each BulkUnitResult where error is absent: available=true iff every date in [start_date, end_date] is available for that unit.
For each BulkUnitResult where error is present: the error describes why that specific unit's lookup failed.
All cache misses triggered by this call have been rebuilt and stored in Redis (unless Redis is unavailable).
Stale bitmasks (anchor_date != today UTC) are rebuilt during this operation.
side_effects: On cache misses: issues batch SELECT queries to PostgreSQL availability_blocks table.
On cache misses: writes rebuilt bitmasks and metadata to Redis via pipeline with configured TTL.
On stale anchor date detection for any unit: deletes and rebuilds those entries.
On Redis failure with fallback enabled: emits a warning-level log and falls back to PostgreSQL for all units.
Singleflight: concurrent misses for the same unit_id within this batch (and across concurrent calls) are coalesced.

functions.name: invalidateCache
functions.description: Deletes the cached bitmask and metadata for a single unit from Redis. The next read for this unit will trigger a lazy rebuild from PostgreSQL. This method is called when availability data is updated (PUT /availability/:unit_id). Invalidation is idempotent: deleting a non-existent key is a successful no-op.

inputs.name: unit_id
inputs.description: The UUID of the unit whose cached bitmask should be invalidated.

validators.error_message: unit_id must be a valid lowercase UUID v4.

error_cases.name: cache_unavailable
error_cases.condition: Redis is unreachable (no fallback for invalidation — must reach Redis to delete the key)

error_cases.name: internal_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected failure during key deletion (e.g., Redis protocol error)

preconditions: unit_id is a valid UUID v4 string.
postconditions: If ok=true, no Redis key exists for this unit_id in the cache (key avail:{CRC32C(unit_id) % shard_count}:{unit_id} has been deleted or did not exist).
If ok=true, the next call to checkAvailability or checkBulkAvailability for this unit_id will trigger a full rebuild from PostgreSQL.
If ok=false with CacheUnavailable, the Redis key may still exist (invalidation failed). Caller should retry or rely on TTL expiry.
side_effects: Deletes the Redis key avail:{CRC32C(unit_id) % shard_count}:{unit_id} if it exists.
May cancel any in-flight singleflight rebuild for this unit_id (implementation-defined).

functions.name: computeShardKey
functions.description: Pure function that computes the ShardKey for a given unit_id. Applies the configured hash algorithm (CRC32C) to the unit_id string and returns the result modulo shard_count. Exposed for testing and observability; not part of the public API.

validators.error_message: unit_id must be a valid lowercase UUID v4.

inputs.name: shard_count
inputs.description: Number of shard buckets. Must match CacheConfig.shard_count.

validators.error_message: Shard count must be between 1 and 1024.
Shard count must be a power of 2.

preconditions: unit_id is a valid UUID v4 string.
shard_count is a positive power of 2.
postconditions: Returned ShardKey is in the range [0, shard_count - 1].
The function is pure: same inputs always produce the same output.
Distribution across shard keys is approximately uniform for random UUID v4 inputs.

functions.name: buildRedisKey
functions.description: Pure function that constructs the full Redis key for a given unit_id. Format: {key_prefix}:{shard_key}:{unit_id}. Exposed for testing and observability; not part of the public API.

validators.error_message: unit_id must be a valid lowercase UUID v4.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Cache configuration providing key_prefix and shard_count.

preconditions: unit_id is a valid UUID v4 string.
postconditions: Returned string matches pattern: {config.key_prefix}:{N}:{unit_id} where N is an integer in [0, config.shard_count - 1].
The function is pure: same inputs always produce the same output.

invariants: The bitmask for a unit is always exactly window_days bits long (default 366 bits). Bit 0 corresponds to today's UTC date; bit N corresponds to today + N days.
A bit value of 1 means the unit is available on that date; a bit value of 0 means the unit is blocked on that date.
'Today' is always defined as the current date at UTC midnight (00:00:00Z). All date arithmetic uses UTC.

The anchor_date stored in BitmaskMetadata must equal today's UTC date for the cached bitmask to be considered valid. If anchor_date != today UTC on a read, the entry is stale and treated as a cache miss.
The Redis key for a unit is always: {key_prefix}:{CRC32C(unit_id) % shard_count}:{unit_id}. This format is immutable for a given CacheConfig.
CRC32C (Castagnoli) is the only supported hash algorithm. The hash is computed over the raw UTF-8 bytes of the unit_id string including hyphens.
Shard count must be a power of 2 to ensure uniform distribution via modulo operation on CRC32C output.
PostgreSQL availability_blocks table is the source of truth. Redis is a derived, read-optimized cache. Any conflict is resolved by rebuilding from PostgreSQL.
All dates in input/output are inclusive on both ends. The range [2024-06-01, 2024-06-03] includes June 1, 2, and 3.
Invalidation is always safe and idempotent. Deleting a non-existent key is a successful no-op.
The singleflight pattern ensures that at most one PostgreSQL query is in-flight at any time for a given unit_id, regardless of concurrent callers.

When Redis is unavailable and fallback_to_pg_on_redis_failure is true, the system operates in degraded mode: all reads go directly to PostgreSQL and no caching occurs. A warning-level log is emitted per request.
Bulk operations preserve input order in results and deduplicate unit_ids. Each unique unit_id appears exactly once in the results.
No method in this component writes to or mutates the PostgreSQL availability_blocks table. This component is read-only with respect to PostgreSQL.
requires: RedisClient implementation must be injected at construction time.
PgClient implementation must be injected at construction time.
CacheConfig must be provided at construction time and is immutable thereafter.
The PostgreSQL availability_blocks table must exist with columns: unit_id (UUID), start_date (DATE), end_date (DATE), is_available (BOOLEAN).
The PostgreSQL units table must exist with a unit_id (UUID) primary key for existence checks.
Redis server must support GETBIT, SETBIT, GETRANGE, DEL, TTL, MULTI/EXEC, and PIPELINE commands.
System clock must be synchronized via NTP for accurate UTC date determination (anchor date correctness depends on this).
